task: A research team wants every paper title from a publications service that returns results a page at a time. Using pages recorded ahead of time, so nothing calls the internet, build a client that reads a page, walks to the last one, reuses pages it has already read, stores the titles in SQLite and prints them A to Z.

produce.name: client.py
produce.about: Reads a page, walks every page, caches pages and stores the titles in SQLite.

produce.name: main.py
produce.about: Collects the titles and prints the count and the sorted list.

steps.P07.m1: Read one recorded page, or an empty list when it wasn't recorded.
steps.P07.m2: Walk the pages from the first until an empty one.
steps.P07.m3: Read each page once and reuse it after that.
steps.P07.m4: Store the titles in SQLite, one row each, and count them.
steps.P07.m5: Print how many titles there are, then the titles A to Z.

problems: Page 3 is empty, which marks the end of the results.
Pages hold different numbers of papers: two on page 1 and one on page 2.
Page numbers are stored as text keys in the file, so a page number has to become text to look the page up.
The titles arrive out of alphabetical order.
